titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§115–120: Sworn Brotherhood Renewed and the Gathering of the Host
part: §§115–120 — Sworn Brotherhood Renewed and the Gathering of the Host
about: Six sections. §115 follows Temüjin, Jamuqa and Qan To'oril as they pull down the Merkid camps and withdraw. §116 tells how the boys Temüjin and Jamuqa first became sworn brothers on the ice of the Onan, with the exchange of knucklebones and arrowheads. §117 has them renew the vow and exchange the belts and horses taken from the Merkid. §118 is the parting at the camp-move, Jamuqa's riddle and Börte-Üjin's reading of it. §119 carries them through the night past the Taichi'ud and gives a boy to Högelün. §120 is a long list of who came to join Temüjin at dawn.

sentences.t: Temüžin Toγ̇oril Qān, Žamuqa γurban qamtudču
sentences.l: Temüžin, To'oril Qān, Žamuqa, three together joining,
sentences.i: Temüjin, Qan To'oril and Jamuqa joined together, the three of them,
sentences.n: A short opening clause with no verb of its own: qamtudču (Ming 相同着, 'together', a converb) hangs on the verb ičuba at the end of unit 3. The subjects are the three men, Temüžin, Toγ̇oril Qān and Žamuqa, and γurban 'three' stands before qamtudču to count them. The title Qān (Ming 皇帝) is the short form beside qaγan and follows the name.
